title: CPU Abstraction
definition: A CPU abstraction is a deliberately simplified architectural model that exposes instructions, selected state, and state-transition rules while hiding implementation detail.
purpose: Enable correct beginner tracing without claiming to reproduce pipelines, caches, speculation, or physical timing.
history: Instruction-set and abstract-machine models separate software-visible behavior from changing processor implementations.
mental_model: A rule executor reads the next instruction and current state, applies the defined transition, and selects the next instruction.
analogy: A clerk following a precise rulebook illustrates architectural behavior; it fails because real processors exploit parallelism and optimization.
common_mistakes: Treating the CPU as understanding human intent
Presenting fetch-decode-execute as a cycle-accurate universal implementation
industry_notes: Instruction-set compatibility permits different processor implementations to expose compatible software-visible behavior.
ai_notes: AI frequently overgeneralizes one processor diagram; verify the abstraction level and target architecture.
interview_notes: Ask which details the model exposes, hides, and cannot justify.
exercise_candidates: Mark architectural versus implementation details in a diagram
lab_candidates: Apply a tiny CPU transition table to an instruction sequence
project_candidates: Write the execution contract for the simulator without hardware-specific claims
